newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Ad agencies J. Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather, both part of the WPP Group, announce they have appointed Bob Zach as worldwide media director for the agencies' Kodak account. Zach was previously executive vice president of Hill Holliday Connors Cosmopulos Boston.

SEOUL - South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co is named a "partner" -- the highest level of corporate sponsorship -- for the 2000 Olympic Games, the International Olympic Committee says. Samsung, the world's largest producer of computer memory chips, was chosen over several other applicants, including Motorola Inc of the United States.

IVANOVO, Russia - Russian newspaper Inform Bazar is doing a roaring trade running classified advertisements from American men seeking Russian wives. Its editor says, "The girls know that Russian men are no good -- no good in bed, no good in life."

GLOUCESTER, Massachusetts - Cyrk Inc, a provider of promotional products and services, says it is merging with privately held Simon Marketing Inc, a Los Angeles-based global promotion agency. Terms of the deal were not disclosed.
SYDNEY - Australian Provincial Newspapers Holdings Ltd acquires the Australian Posters outdoor advertising division from 3M Australia Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - Consumers will soon be able to surf the Internet on their televisions, shop, and do their banking, as well as watching their favourite soap operas. But analysts doubt there will be a great clamour any time soon for interactive TV, unless new services are more exciting, useful or cheap.

TOKYO - Aggressive U.S. moves to enter the digital TV market have alarmed Japan into rushing ahead with its own plans, which it hopes will make up for lost time and create opportunities for Japanese manufacturers, industry experts say.
DALLAS - ABC Radio Networks says it plans to move forward with a national rollout of Radio Disney, a network geared toward children and family-oriented programming.

WARSAW - French firm Hachette has asked a Warsaw court to rule whether its initial deal to buy press chain Ruch SA, signed in December with the treasury ministry but later annulled, is legally binding, PAP news agency says.

PARIS - Cable television is watched in 23.8 percent of the homes in France that are equipped to receive cable TV, a figure that has increased in the last two years, according to Mediametrie, an audience measurement body.
TOKYO - Japan's Fuji Television says it has been asked by Japan Sky Broadcasting Corp to take a stake in the satellite broadcasting venture, but adds that no agreement has yet been reached.

SYDNEY - James Packer, son of billionaire businessman Kerry Packer and managing director of the family's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, says Australian media rules should not continue to prevent the company from bidding for newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd. "Why shouldn't we be allowed to buy Fairfax, an Australian newspaper company, and grow our business?," he says in an interview on the Nine Network's A Current Affair programme.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW YORK - McDonald's Corp hasn't achieved the kind of sales boost it was looking for by reducing the price of its hallmark Big Mac sandwiches 75 percent to 55 cents, according to the Wall Street Journal.

LONDON - Increasingly competitive retail markets are spurring owners of brand-name products to zealously protect their brands, and marketing experts say no brand can afford to drop its guard. "Brands have to be constantly nourished," Alan Watson, chairman of marketing and communication firm Burson-Marsteller Europe, says. "The moment you've established a brand, you are on a treadmill. You have to promote it, innovate it." *********
ROME - Italian new car registrations rose 52.37 percent to 231,500 units in April, compared with 151,933 in April 1996, the Ministry of Transport says.

ZAGREB - Representatives of Hilton hotels have visited Croatia's capital and famous walled coastal city of Dubrovnik and are expected to expand into the Croatian market soon, Tourism Ministry hotel expert Davor Njiric says.
TOKYO - Riding high on extremely strong sales of its cutting-edge PlayStation game console, Sony Corp is seen as replacing Nintendo Co Ltd as the king of the home videogame market, analysts say.
LONDON - Environmentally-friendly cosmetics retailer Body Shop International Plc says it is in talks with a number of major French retailers to take over franchising for its stores in France.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - China's cosmetics market is expected to grow 22 percent a year through the year 2001, as personal incomes continue to rise and taboos against cosmetics disappear, market research group Datamonitor says.
LONDON - Britons are stressed out, confused about what to eat and know they should exercise but don't, a survey published by the Office for National Statistics says.
